newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish PM says full employment next target-paper.
newsitem.headline: Swedish PM says full employment next target-paper.

text.p: Sweden's Prime Minister Goran Persson aims for full employment after reaching his goal to halve unemployment to four percent at the turn of the century, tabloid Aftonbladet reported on Wednesday.
"Open unemployment should be halved by the year 2000," Persson and Bertil Jonsson, leader of the blue collar labour union umbrella LO, wrote in a comment in Aftonbladet.
"When that target has been reached we must move on to full employment."
Combatting unemployment should not have a negative impact on the favourable business climate or on state finances, which need to be strong, they said.
"...Full employment with a strong common economy and secure welfare is the best for Sweden," they said.
"We dismiss the view that unemployment is needed to fight inflation."
To reach the target of full employment it is essential that inflation is kept at bay also after the year 2000. Therefore, wage increases cannot be higher than in other European countries, they said.
"A united labour movement that takes responsibility for both politics and wage formation can succeed in what no other country has managed -- reaching full employmnent," they said.
